summary: Dedicated (A100 80GB, TP=4) intermittent tensor-parallel hangs causing streaming timeouts (Acme AI)
environment: prod / us-east (Dedicated VPC) / runtime 1.18.x (customer pinned) / A100 80GB
description:
Issue summary
- Customer (Acme AI, Dedicated) reports intermittent hangs on multi-GPU tensor-parallel replicas (A100 80GB, TP=4) that present as streaming requests timing out. When the hang occurs, affected replicas stop making forward progress; queued requests back up; downstream app sees elevated p99 and repeated client-side timeouts.

Impact
- Customer-facing: streaming responses stall mid-generation; client disconnects at ~60–180s depending on their gateway timeout.
- Platform: p99 latency spikes, retry storms, autoscaling churn (adds capacity but stuck replicas remain in rotation unless drained).
- Incident classification: Sev1 (enterprise Dedicated), started 2025-02-17.

Customer symptoms (from Acme)
- “Some requests never finish. They stream a few tokens and then hang until our 120s timeout.”
- Happens more during peak traffic and mixed workload (short prompts + long prompts, concurrent streams).

Environment
- Dedicated deployment: Acme AI (us-east), A100 80GB.
- Replica topology: TP=4, 1 replica = 4 GPUs.
- Runtime: 1.18.x (pinned) with CUDA graphs enabled.
- Traffic pattern: bursty concurrency, mixed prefill/decode, long contexts (~8k–16k) present during peak.

What we’ve observed (initial triage)
- Symptoms match known “TP silent stall” signatures: GPU utilization drops on one rank; other ranks appear blocked; no hard NCCL error surfaces to API.
- Request traces show decode iteration stops advancing; stream remains open; eventually customer gateway times out.
- At least 2 occurrences correlate with high prefill load on the same replica prior to stall.

Reproduction status
- Not yet deterministic in customer environment. Runtime team has a similar repro in progress using mixed prompt lengths + streaming decode.

Logs / signals (snippets)
- Customer-provided (sanitized) streaming timeout logs:
  - 2025-02-17T19:44:12Z request_id=rw_01HR… model=llama3-70b tp=4 stream=true status=client_timeout duration_ms=120000 tokens_out=214
- Redwood replica logs (sanitized, from us-east dedicated cluster):
  - [rank=2] WARN tp_step stalled: last_progress_ms=93210 in_flight_collectives=all_reduce:7 all_gather:3 scheduler_q_depth=128 stall_hint=collective_wait
  - [rank=0] INFO decode_loop: waiting on barrier event=tp_sync_42 stream=decode
- NCCL debug (after enabling extra logging window):
  - NCCL WARN Async operation in progress, stream=comm, opCount=1193 (no subsequent completion)

Immediate mitigations recommended (customer + SRE)
- Drain/replace suspect replicas when heartbeat gap/timeout spike detected.
- Reduce max concurrency per replica (cap inflight streams) and cap max batch tokens.
- Temporarily disable CUDA graphs for TP replicas (reduces performance, improves debuggability; recommended during incident).
- Enable safer scheduling guardrail flag (prefill/decode fairness) if available in pinned runtime.

Links
- Incident Slack: #incidents thread 1740165551-sev1-dedicated-timeouts-suspected-tp-hang
- Eng runtime threads: 1739812205-nccl-collective-ordering-suspected-mismatch; 1739973309-watchdog-default-timeout-values
- Internal runbook: Confluence “runtime-tp-hang-mitigation”

Ask / next steps
- Need runtime engineering to confirm likely root cause category (scheduler starvation vs NCCL ordering vs cancel path) and provide near-term fix/flag recommendation compatible with Acme’s pinned version.
- Need SRE to add temporary alerting on TP heartbeat gaps for Acme’s Dedicated cluster and automate drain on stall detection where safe.

Account context
- Acme AI is in active expansion; this is blocking a production rollout unless we can reduce timeouts to near-zero at peak. Customer requested ETA for fix and recommended settings for peak traffic.

resolution: Resolved via mitigations and operational controls while fixes are prepared for runtime 1.19: (1) reduced concurrency and batch aggressiveness, (2) temporarily disabled CUDA graphs on TP replicas, (3) enabled additional NCCL debug logging during a short window, and (4) added SRE automation to drain replicas on TP heartbeat gaps. Permanent fixes tracked in ENG-4821 initiative and related PRs (scheduler fairness/collective ordering, NCCL stream/event sync hardening, TP watchdog + safe abort/drain, improved error surfacing). Customer aligned on a Dedicated-first canary rollout plan for runtime 1.19.
